title: Scary Movie 4
synopsis: Aliens. Ghosts. A grim village. A hand reaching out of the well. Also somebody on a unicycle for no reason. Welcome to the parody — pick the dumbest possible choice and probably live.

nodes.text: An ominous tripod legs over your fence. Your neighbor Tom screams artistically. A baby in a stroller deadlifts a chainsaw. You're holding a TV remote and a half-eaten waffle. The paths divide here: “Brandish the waffle” leads into The Basement, while “Run dramatically in slow motion” makes The Grim Village the next reckoning.

choices.consequence: Absurdity is a shield in this universe. You commit to brandish the waffle. It carries you into The Basement while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
You commit to run dramatically in slow motion. It carries you into The Grim Village while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You hide in the basement, which has, inexplicably, a karaoke machine and three life-size mannequins of yourself. One of them is doing your taxes. To choose “Sing karaoke at the tripod” means meeting Brenda's Apartment; “Fight your tax-doing doppelganger” sends you toward Tom Ryan's Crane instead.

choices.consequence: Distract aliens with American Idol. You choose to sing karaoke at the tripod. By Brenda's Apartment, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.
Self-loathing made literal. You choose to fight your tax-doing doppelganger. By Tom Ryan's Crane, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You sprint and accidentally arrive in a black-and-white village from a completely different horror movie. The elders look at you suspiciously. There is a strict no-shoes policy. “Bow to the elders” opens the route to Brenda's Apartment. “Eat the forbidden grapes immediately” changes the terms and carries you toward Tom Ryan's Crane.

choices.consequence: When in spoof, do as the spoof does. You commit to bow to the elders. It carries you into Brenda's Apartment while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
Curiosity killed the parody. You choose to eat the forbidden grapes immediately. By Tom Ryan's Crane, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Brenda is hiding from a ghost-cousin and watching the news, which is just a guy in glasses yelling about cats. The ghost rises from her TV in 480i resolution. To choose “Throw popcorn at the ghost” means meeting The Town Meeting; “Negotiate with the ghost about residuals” sends you toward The Iron Lung instead.

choices.consequence: Snacks are weapons here. You throw popcorn at the ghost. The way toward The Town Meeting opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Negotiate with the ghost about residuals

The paths divide here: “Climb the crane to help” leads into The Town Meeting, while “Stay on the ground and yell back” makes The Iron Lung the next reckoning.

nodes.text: The aliens, it turns out, are scared of love. Brenda and you, holding hands while delivering a monologue, are functionally a nuke. The tripod tilts toward you, weeping politely. To choose “Hug the alien” means meeting Brenda's Speech; “Begin a wedding flash mob” sends you toward Tom Ryan, Hero? instead.

choices.consequence: Hugs solve everything in spoof. You commit to hug the alien. It carries you into Brenda's Speech while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You're absorbed into the tripod. Inside, it's a Costco. The aliens are buying bulk humans for snacks. You sneak into the sample aisle as a disguise. Choose “Sample your way to the controls” and Brenda's Speech comes into view; choose “Convince the aliens to give up snacks for Lent” and the road bends toward Tom Ryan, Hero?.

nodes.text: Brenda gives a Best Original Speech that makes the aliens cry chrome tears. The tripods all sit down in formation. Earth's anthem plays through three different car alarms. “Kiss Brenda for the credits” draws you toward Roll Credits; “Crown Brenda president immediately” leaves President Brenda waiting on the other side.

choices.consequence: Spoof endings demand it. You commit to kiss Brenda for the credits. It carries you into Roll Credits while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.
Bypass the constitution by applause. You crown Brenda president immediately. The way toward President Brenda opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Tom Ryan, despite being absolutely no good at parenting, manages to defeat the lead alien by accident with a beer bong and a leaf blower. His son slow-claps with the propeller hat still spinning. To choose “Let Tom take the credit” means meeting End-Credit Scene Setup; “Steal the credit on live TV” sends you toward Karma, in Stilettos instead.

choices.consequence: Sometimes the doofus wins. You let Tom take the credit. The way toward End-Credit Scene Setup opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Steal the credit on live TV
choices.consequence: Karma takes a sick day in spoofs. You commit to steal the credit on live TV. It carries you into Karma, in Stilettos while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The threat is over. A second tripod ominously rises behind you. Then a third. Then a fourth, which is just a person on stilts who's late to the bit. The paths divide here: “Run for a sequel hook” leads into The Cameo, while “Decide not to look back” makes Walk-Off Joke the next reckoning.

choices.consequence: You commit to run for a sequel hook. It carries you into The Cameo while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: You and Brenda, three years later, are at a kids' birthday party. The clown is, suspiciously, an alien in a hat. Nobody is paying attention. You smile, because that's the joke. The paths divide here: “Wink at the camera” leads into Love Wins, Stupidly, while “Eat cake and ignore the alien” makes Tom Ryan, Lord and Savior the next reckoning.

choices.consequence: Fourth-wall break for the road. You commit to wink at the camera. It carries you into Love Wins, Stupidly while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.consequence: Be the calm in the spoof. You eat cake and ignore the alien. The way toward Tom Ryan, Lord and Savior opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The credits roll on you and Brenda waving from a parade float made of taxi roof signs. Critics call it 'the dumbest defeat of evil in cinema history,' which the marketing team prints on the poster verbatim.

Brenda is sworn in. Her first executive order is mandatory karaoke Tuesdays. Approval ratings hit 93%. The aliens write a strongly-worded letter and then visit on vacation. The road into President Brenda began with “Crown Brenda president immediately” in Brenda's Speech; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Tom is celebrated worldwide for accidentally winning a war. He sells autographs at fairs. His son finally takes off the propeller hat. You are happy for them in a slightly bewildered way. The road into Tom Ryan, Lord and Savior began with “Eat cake and ignore the alien” in Bonus Scene; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You take the credit on live TV. Within six minutes you're trending for the wrong reasons. Your reputation is repaired only after a heartfelt podcast apology and a charity bake sale. The road into Karma, in Stilettos began with “Steal the credit on live TV” in Tom Ryan, Hero?; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

A title card promises 'Scary Movie 5: This Time It's Personal-er.' Nobody asked. Everyone shows up anyway. Spoofs, like cockroaches, survive everything. The road into To Be Continued (Loosely) began with “Give them the closing line” in The Cameo; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You walk into the sunset which is, on closer inspection, a painted sheet held up by two stagehands. One of them shrugs. You shrug back. Roll credits. The road into Walk-Off Joke began with “Decide not to look back” in End-Credit Scene Setup; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
